dispositions.span_text: Bellicum will reimburse Miltenyi for Third Party royalties and/or license fees, if any, owed by Miltenyi under Third Party license agreements existing as of the Effective Date as set forth on Exhibit D solely to the extent Miltenyi's exercise of rights under such licenses is required 27 Miltenyi Biotec-Bellicum Supply Agreement (Execution Copy, March 27, 2019) to supply Miltenyi Product to Bellicum under this Agreement for the Permitted Use; and further provided that amounts owed under such Third Party license agreements have not otherwise been passed through to Bellicum and are actually paid by Miltenyi to Miltenyi's licensor(s).

Bellicum acknowledges that the potential volume of such Third Party royalties and/or license fees under applicable Third Party license agreements will be as set forth on Exhibit D, as updated from time to time by Miltenyi.
dispositions.reason: ‘Bellicum acknowledges that ... will be as set forth on Exhibit D’ states a future FACT about what an exhibit will say, not a party's undertaking -- §3.2's own 'will'-ambiguity rule: 'will' is not an obligation at all when it states a future fact about the agreement ('this Agreement will terminate on...'); this is the identical shape one level removed via an acknowledgment. Matches §2.7's own text naming 'an acknowledgment' as a no-modal-verb class alongside a rights-reservation and a copular status clause.

dispositions.span_text: If, during the Term of this Agreement, the Parties mutually agree to obtain additional Third Party licenses to enable the Permitted Use of Miltenyi Products by Bellicum, its Affiliates, Subcontractors, and/or Licensees under this Agreement, and such additional licenses give rise to Third Party royalties and/or license fees with respect to Bellicum's use of Miltenyi Products under this Agreement, then the Parties will negotiate in good faith which Party(ies) is/are responsible for payment of such Third Party royalties and/or license fees.
Miltenyi, acting reasonably, reserves the right to defer the inclusion of additional Miltenyi Products in Exhibit B hereto until the Parties have reached agreement on this matter.

dispositions.reason: Surplus clause #1 -- "Miltenyi, acting reasonably, reserves the right to defer the inclusion of additional Miltenyi Products in Exhibit B hereto until the Parties have reached agreement on this matter". ELIGIBLE. RULED 2026-09-05 -- SPLITTING_EXCLUSION_INVESTIGATION.md DECISION 3, written into the guideline as section 10.2 (general retroactivity policy, v0.52). THIS SPAN IS ELIGIBLE. Part 1 of the section 10.2 test: section 2.5 says of ITSELF that it clarifies what section 2's own exclusion row already meant and does not add a new criterion, so it reaches items stamped at any version -- the rule it clarifies was already in force at v0.28. BUT THE RETROACTIVITY ANSWER DOES NOT ACTUALLY DECIDE THIS SPAN, AND THAT IS WHY IT WAS A SAFE CASE TO SETTLE THE GENERAL POLICY ON: section 2's exclusion row is SEGMENT-level and gated on the word 'only' ('Contains ONLY a party's right with no correlative duty'), and this segment carries annotated duties, so that row could not reach this clause at v0.28 either. Section 2.6's sentence-granularity ruling is itself v0.41. Both branches therefore converge on ANNOTATE: if section 2.5 reaches back, the clause CLEARS its monitorable-stakes test (settled concordantly by two independent annotators, C14_076_INVESTIGATION.md section 7.2); if it does not, no v0.28 rule excluded the clause at all. The 'pre-section-2.5 practice never annotated a bare MAY/option clause' reading is a description of PRACTICE, not a rule, and section 2.1's bias safeguard and section 14.4 both refuse to treat an unrecorded practice as a disposition. DISCLOSED AGAINST INTEREST BEFORE THE RULING, per section 10.2 part 3: the model's predictions for this span were measured first and they cut AGAINST adding it -- see this entry's prediction_disclosure field. Adding the item can only LOWER criterion 2, which is the monotone direction section 10.2 part 3 permits without freeze-pass protection.

CORROBORATED 2026-09-05, near-verbatim: the cold annotator reached this reading independently and CONFIDENT, listing the IDENTICAL THREE STAKES IN THE SAME ORDER ('acting reasonably' as section 2.5.1's own counter-example to 'sole business judgment'; the bounded observable end-point 'until the Parties have reached agreement'; the narrow specific object against C04-026's ten-verb catch-all) and independently distinguishing section 2.5.1's C14-044 negative example on the same ground. Cold additionally reaches a field this reading does not: temporal RELATIVE_TO_TRIGGER(before, 'the Parties have reached agreement on this matter') with known_gaps ['relative_trigger_preposition'], per section 8.9's v0.34 correction that 'until' was never counted but IS covered by the rule as written -- and section 8.9's own cassette observation records 'until <trigger>' occurring in C04-117 twice, which is this sentence. NARROWED SCOPE: the SUBSTANTIVE question is settled concordantly; what remains is DECISION 3 ALONE -- retroactivity over a segment locked at v0.28 (C04-01 stamps v0.28; section 2.5 is v0.39, section 2.5.1 is v0.41). One Decision 3 ruling disposes of both this span and C11-094 #3. CAVEAT per section 7.1: concordance is a LOWER BOUND on error, not proof.
